title: Trustworthy Machine Learning via Memorization and the Granular Long-Tail: A Survey on Interactions, Tradeoffs, and Beyond

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying literature on how long-tailed data distributions and class imbalances cause models to favor majority classes while underperforming on minority (tail) classes, and analyzing the trade-offs of using re-sampling, re-weighting, and focal loss strategies.

Reviewing standard group fairness metrics (e.g., Demographic Parity, Equalized Odds, Equal Opportunity) and evaluating how interventions like Differential Privacy (DP-SGD) and Adversarial Training disproportionately degrade accuracy and utility for minority demographic groups.

Analyzing existing studies on multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) to compare safety vulnerabilities (e.g., jailbreaks), hallucination rates, and overall performance disparities between high-resource languages and underrepresented, low-resource languages.
